course.name: Kaizen
course.tagline: A crypto trading and education community founded by YouTuber Brian Jung, combining 20+ analysts with structured educational guides.
course.about: Kaizen is a crypto trading community founded by Brian Jung, a YouTube creator and entrepreneur. It combines 20+ expert analysts and researchers with educational resources — including a crypto terms glossary and a crypto trading basics section covering exchanges, regulation, leverage and spot vs. futures trading — alongside daily alerts and weekly livestreams.

formats.label: Daily alerts & livestreams
formats.description: Daily crypto alerts and weekly livestreams with 20+ analysts.

formats.label: Educational guides
formats.description: "Crypto Trading Basics" and a "Crypto Key Terms" glossary.

formats.label: Discord community
formats.description: A 20,000+ member Discord with portfolio-review opportunities and a beginner FAQ channel.

formats.label: Kaizen Jobs
formats.description: A section listing work opportunities in the crypto sector.

pricing.name: Lite
pricing.billing_note: Community Discord and Whop access; excludes premium alerts, calls and livestreams.

course.testimonials_note: We couldn't find any individually-quoted member testimonials for this community in the sources we could access, so none are shown here. Worth knowing: a couple of third-party review round-ups mention members being encouraged to leave 5-star reviews in exchange for extra content, which may affect how representative the Whop rating is — we haven't independently confirmed this.

_notes.source: Founder (Brian Jung) and most structural detail confirmed via Whop's own blog review (whop.com/blog/kaizen-review) and WebSearch results. Pricing (Lite $7/wk, Platinum $199/mo, $550/3mo, $1,075/6mo, $2,000/yr) from the same sources, not independently re-verified against the live Whop checkout. Trustpilot (4.6/5, 72 reviews, Excellent) confirmed directly for thekaizen.co. Logo is the community's own square icon from its Whop profile. Review-incentive concern noted above comes from a single third-party review round-up, not corroborated elsewhere — flagged for transparency, not presented as confirmed fact.
